assets.researchSummary: Bittensor's engineering cadence stays fast, with v495 live two days after runtime 494 and the 160-subnet cap. assets.overview: Bittensor's payments, distribution and security story all moved this month. Gamma Tokens went live network-wide on Nov 9–10, letting wallets and AI agents pay for one subnet's services with dollar-valued credits minted by burning that subnet's alpha, and runtime 491 (Nov 16) added Gamma controls to the SDK and btcli. The Chutes inference subnet (SN64) signed Alibaba Cloud on Nov 17, a week after Tencent Cloud. Post-quantum ML-DSA and Falcon wallets are now switched on for mainnet (reported Nov 18), and runtime 492, live on Nov 19, tightened coldkey and hotkey swap rules and limited elevated transaction priority to the sudo key, with no fee changes. The main risk is adoption: subnets must opt in to Gamma, the cloud deals have no disclosed revenue, and post-quantum accounts depend on wallet support. On Nov 23 the subnet cap rose from 128 to 160 with the emission gate moved to rank 48, and runtime 494 (burn-for-commit, weight delegation, basket controls; transaction version 2) is live on mainnet. Subtensor v495, published Nov 24, enlarges Null-consensus subnets, opens Gamma deposits for subnet owners without a pause and sizes root claims per validator. Runtime v495 went live on Nov 25 while community channels disputed the Nov 23 subnet-cap increase; the team proposed GitHub-based sign-off for sudo-level changes.

marketAlerts.change: Bullpen confirms unauthorized transfers from 18–19 early-beta accounts, including Ansem's Solana wallet; about $2.57 million traced to Arbitrum
marketAlerts.summary: Trading terminal Bullpen said that on Nov 24 it identified unauthorized transfers involving accounts opened during its April–June 2024 early beta, with a preliminary count of 18–19 affected accounts including that of co-founder and trader Ansem. Bullpen lets users import existing wallets by private key, and Ansem said attackers reached his Bullpen profile, which held his Solana wallet's imported key, and sold his meme-coin holdings. Onchain investigators traced about $2.57 million in proceeds to a wallet on Arbitrum, according to Decrypt. Bullpen took the affected test service offline and says no other users' funds were affected; the root cause has not been published.
marketAlerts.why: It is a custody-design incident rather than a Solana protocol flaw: any app that stores imported private keys becomes a single point of failure for those wallets. Users of trading terminals that hold imported keys should review exposure until Bullpen publishes how access was gained.

marketAlerts.change: Braiins discloses BGP route hijacks that diverted hashrate from 1,000+ bitcoin mining sites on unencrypted Stratum V1 connections
marketAlerts.summary: Mining pool operator Braiins published a security alert on Nov 25 saying an attacker forged internet routes to redirect miners using plain-text Stratum V1 connections to an impostor pool. On Nov 20 more than a thousand mining sites across hundreds of networks were redirected in the same second; earlier episodes from Nov 7–12 hit mainly Latin American sites. Braiins says neither its pool nor the miners were breached, pool accounts and payouts were unaffected, and the attack remains a live threat to any pool accepting unencrypted Stratum V1. It urges miners to move to Stratum V2 or certificate-verified TLS and network operators to enable RPKI route-origin validation.
marketAlerts.why: It shows a long-known weakness in bitcoin mining connections being exploited at scale, with stolen hashrate rather than stolen coins as the loss. The fixes exist but depend on miners, firmware makers and ISPs adopting them.

marketAlerts.change: Bithumb widens its October breach disclosure: IDs, bank accounts and wallet addresses exposed, with access lasting Oct 12–27
marketAlerts.summary: South Korea's second-largest exchange Bithumb updated its disclosure on Nov 25 about the October breach of its DaouOffice groupware. It now says unauthorized access lasted from Oct 12 to Oct 27, not about an hour as first reported, and that exposed data includes ID and passport or driver's-licence numbers, bank account details, ID copies, transaction records and crypto wallet addresses. Bithumb did not give a revised count of affected people; it is notifying them individually and warned of follow-on phishing. No loss of customer crypto has been reported.
marketAlerts.why: Leaked identity and wallet data makes targeted phishing against Korean users more likely, and it lands as Korea drafts exchange liability rules. It is a data breach, not a theft of funds.

marketAlerts.change: South Korea's FSC unveils a draft Digital Asset Act that would allow domestic ICOs with white-paper filings, license stablecoin issuers and cap exchange ownership at 20%
marketAlerts.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission presented a draft 'Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users' at its virtual-asset committee on Nov 24. The draft would allow domestic token sales again if issuers file a white paper with the FSC before soliciting buyers, followed by a cooling-off period, and would require exchanges to publish disclosures for listed assets. Won stablecoins would need FSC authorization, at least ₩5 billion in capital and 100% reserves held at banks, with bank-majority consortia allowed to issue first. Exchange shareholders would be capped at 20% (up to 34% with approval) after a three-year grace period, and exchanges would face no-fault liability for hacks; the bill still needs National Assembly passage.
marketAlerts.why: Korea is one of the largest retail crypto markets, and lifting the nine-year ICO ban while regulating listings and stablecoins would reshape how tokens reach Korean users. The ownership cap could force Upbit and Bithumb shareholders to restructure, so the legislative path is worth tracking.

marketAlerts.change: US Justice Department files to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC tied to the Oct 29 Binance hack; Circle agrees to reissue tokens after a forfeiture order
marketAlerts.summary: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint on Nov 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Oct 29 Binance hack, which US officials attribute to North Korea's Lazarus Group / APT38. The complaint identifies 36 addresses across 18 blockchains holding frozen funds. Because Circle cannot move tokens out of blocklisted addresses, it agreed to issue replacement USDC once a court enters a forfeiture order. Binance separately hired Mandiant, SlowMist and Verichains for independent security reviews.
marketAlerts.why: It is one of the largest crypto forfeiture actions on record and shows freezable stablecoins becoming the main recovery path after state-linked hacks. Any return to Binance or victims still depends on the court process.

marketAlerts.change: Upbit and Bithumb designate Sky's SKY and the USDS stablecoin as trading-caution assets and suspend deposits pending a Dec 21–24 review
marketAlerts.summary: Upbit and Bithumb both designated SKY and USDS as caution assets effective 8 PM KST on Nov 23 (5 AM CST), suspending deposits across their KRW, BTC and USDT pairs. Upbit cited the issuing and operating parties' capability, credibility and disclosure, while Bithumb cited business substance, sustainability and operator reliability. The action follows a Nov 19 Inca Digital report, published via CoinDesk, linking about $518 million of Peg Stability Module flows to wallets tied to hackers and sanctioned actors, which Sky disputes as about 0.03% of PSM volume. Both exchanges will decide between lifting the designation, extending it or ending trading support during Dec 21–24; USDS has held its peg, and DAXA has issued no joint notice.
marketAlerts.why: A delisting of a top-five dollar stablecoin on Korea's two largest exchanges would be a notable precedent for compliance screening of DeFi stablecoins. It is a caution flag, not a delisting, and no depeg has occurred.

marketAlerts.change: Franklin Templeton's US-listed EZPZ crypto index ETF will add HYPE on or about Dec 1
marketAlerts.summary: A Nov 25 prospectus supplement says CF Benchmarks will add Hyperliquid's HYPE to the CF Institutional Digital Asset Index on Dec 1, and that the Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will hold it from on or about that date. EZPZ will then hold bitcoin, ether, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, Cardano, Stellar and HYPE at roughly their index weights. The fund relies on Cboe BZX's SEC-approved generic listing standards to add constituents. HYPE's weight was not disclosed.
marketAlerts.why: It is the first US-listed ETF set to hold HYPE, a step past the non-US products launched this month. The weight is index-driven and undisclosed, so the flow impact cannot be sized.

marketAlerts.change: Hong Kong's HKMA launches the CMU Digital Asset Platform for tokenized debt securities
marketAlerts.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the official launch of the CMU Digital Asset Platform on Nov 25, a DLT-based system run by CMU OmniClear for issuing, clearing, settling, paying coupons on and redeeming debt securities, including tokenized traditional bonds. It settles atomically on-chain delivery-versus-payment, connects directly to RTGS systems and CBDCs, and supports 24-hour multi-currency settlement with cash tokens. Ten banks were onboarded as first direct participants. CMU OmniClear plans to extend it to funds and real-world assets and to connect tokenized deposits and regulated stablecoins.
marketAlerts.why: Central-bank-run settlement rails for tokenized bonds make Hong Kong one of the first jurisdictions with production tokenization infrastructure at the market core. It is a permissioned platform, so public-chain links remain a future step.

marketAlerts.change: SEC staff give Molecule no-action relief to sell research 'Project Tokens' without registration
marketAlerts.summary: The SEC's Division of Corporation Finance said on Nov 24 it would not recommend enforcement if Molecule's US subsidiary LabsCo offers and sells Project Tokens as described, without registering them under Section 5 or Section 12(g). The tokens give research participation and only non-binding votes on research direction, with no ownership, profit or equity rights, and locking them does not create a financial interest. The relief rests on the facts in Molecule's Nov 19 request and is not a legal conclusion. Molecule said its first project will use the model in the coming weeks.
marketAlerts.why: It is another staff-level template for issuing consumptive tokens in the US without registration, alongside earlier no-action letters. It binds only on the stated facts, so it is a signal rather than a rule.

marketAlerts.change: ECB will accept securities issued on DLT Pilot Regime platforms as Eurosystem collateral, with implementation planned for June 2027
marketAlerts.summary: The ECB Governing Council approved accepting marketable assets issued on DLT platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime as collateral for Eurosystem credit operations, announced Nov 23. Assets must meet standard eligibility rules and reach the Eurosystem through an eligible CSD link that settles in TARGET2-Securities. Platform requirements on settlement finality and outsourcing will be published in spring 2027, with implementation planned for June 2027. Assets issued and settled entirely on DLT networks are not yet covered.
marketAlerts.why: Central-bank collateral eligibility is one of the strongest incentives for banks to issue tokenized securities in Europe. It is scheduled, not in force, and does not cover crypto assets.

news.title: Franklin Templeton's US-listed EZPZ crypto index ETF will add HYPE on or about Dec 1
news.body: A prospectus supplement filed with the SEC on Nov 25 says CF Benchmarks will add Hyperliquid's HYPE to the CF Institutional Digital Asset Index on Dec 1, and the Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will hold it from on or about that date. EZPZ will then hold bitcoin, ether, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, Cardano, Stellar and HYPE at roughly their index weights, rebalanced quarterly. The fund relies on Cboe BZX's SEC-approved generic listing standards, so no separate approval is needed to add the constituent. HYPE's starting weight was not disclosed. It follows Brazil's HYPH11 listing on B3 a day earlier.
news.why: It is the first US-listed ETF set to hold HYPE, giving US brokerage investors indirect exposure even though Hyperliquid itself restricts US users. The weight is index-driven and undisclosed, so the size of any flow cannot be estimated.
news.tagReason: First US-listed ETF to include HYPE.
news.summary: A prospectus supplement filed with the SEC on Nov 25 says CF Benchmarks will add Hyperliquid's HYPE to the CF Institutional Digital Asset Index on Dec 1, and the Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will hold it from on or about that date.

news.title: Solana activates account data direct mapping on mainnet, ending per-instruction account copies
news.body: Anza said the account_data_direct_mapping feature gate would activate on Solana mainnet at epoch 1097, around 3:50 PM CST on Nov 25, and Solana's developer account confirmed that evening that direct mapping is live. Validators no longer copy account data into the program VM and back for every instruction and cross-program call, which Anza says speeds replay and block production for CPI-heavy transactions and large accounts. The stricter memory checks that can break unsafe programs were already active, and nothing changes for app users. Anza calls it the prerequisite for SIMD-0268, which would raise CPI nesting depth from 4 to 8; that change has no date yet. Solana also relaunched its developer docs and introduced Solana Playground, a browser IDE with an AI assistant, on Nov 25.
news.why: It completes a runtime change four years in the making and removes a real execution bottleneck, without needing a client switch. Programs that relied on old memory behaviour were the risk, and those checks went live earlier.
news.tagReason: Core runtime upgrade live on mainnet.

news.title: Hong Kong's HKMA launches the CMU Digital Asset Platform to issue and settle tokenized bonds
news.body: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the official launch of the CMU Digital Asset Platform on Nov 25, run by CMU OmniClear on its behalf. The DLT-based platform covers issuance, settlement of secondary trades, coupon payments and redemption of debt securities, including tokenized traditional bonds. It settles atomically on-chain delivery-versus-payment, connects directly to RTGS systems and central bank digital currencies, and supports 24-hour multi-currency settlement with cash tokens. Ten banks were onboarded as the first direct participants, and CMU OmniClear plans to extend it to funds and real-world assets and to link tokenized deposits and regulated stablecoins.
news.why: A central-bank-run settlement layer for tokenized bonds puts Hong Kong among the first markets with production tokenization at its core. It is permissioned, so links to public chains are a later step.
news.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the official launch of the CMU Digital Asset Platform on Nov 25, run by CMU OmniClear on its behalf.

news.title: XRPL's Single Asset Vault amendment gains majority and starts its two-week countdown; the Lending Protocol needs one more vote
news.body: The SingleAssetVault amendment (XLS-65) reached majority on the XRP Ledger at 1:38 PM CST on Nov 25, with 29 of 35 trusted validators in favour. If support stays above 80% for 14 days, it activates on Dec 9. The companion LendingProtocol amendment (XLS-66) stands at 28 of 35, exactly 80%, so it needs one more yes vote before its own countdown can start. Flare said on Nov 25 that its XRPL validator voted yes on XLS-66. Both amendments are needed for native lending on the ledger.
news.why: Vaults plus lending would give XRP and RLUSD native on-ledger credit markets, a long-awaited DeFi capability. A single validator dropping out resets the clock, so Dec 9 is conditional.

news.title: Bittensor's runtime v495 goes live as the subnet-cap backlash continues; the team proposes GitHub-based sign-off for sudo changes
news.body: Subtensor v495 went live on Nov 25, letting Null-consensus subnets run up to 16 mechanisms under a shared epoch with a UID budget of 2,500 that is split across mechanisms, opening Gamma deposits to subnet owners and sizing root claims per validator. Community channels welcomed the release but spent the day disputing the Nov 23 decision to raise the subnet cap from 128 to 160 and widen emissions to the top 48 subnets, arguing it fragments subnet liquidity. In response, the team proposed routing sudo-level upgrades through GitHub merges tied to the chain; members said a credible delay would have to be enforced on-chain. The cap and emission gate are unchanged.
news.why: The runtime work extends what subnets can run, but the governance argument is the bigger signal: changes that move emissions are still made by sudo, and holders want a predictable process. No formal governance change has been adopted yet.
news.summary: Subtensor v495 went live on Nov 25, letting Null-consensus subnets run up to 16 mechanisms under a shared epoch with a UID budget of 2,500 that is split across mechanisms, opening Gamma deposits to subnet owners and sizing root claims per validator.

news.title: Ethereum-native USDT goes live on Axelar for cross-chain transfers
news.body: Axelar said on Nov 25 that Tether's Ethereum USDT contract is now live on its network, so the token can be moved from Ethereum to other Axelar-connected chains. Axelar described it as the world's largest stablecoin moving seamlessly across chains and pointed users to its transfer app. No volume, fee or route details were published, and Tether did not issue a statement of its own.
news.why: Adding the largest stablecoin is one of the most useful routes an interoperability network can offer, and it supports demand for Axelar's message and gas services. Usage will matter more than the listing, and Tether's own USDT0 network competes for the same flows.
news.summary: Axelar said on Nov 25 that Tether's Ethereum USDT contract is now live on its network, so the token can be moved from Ethereum to other Axelar-connected chains.

news.title: VeChain says WanBridge will shut as early as Dec 31; holders of bridged assets must unwrap by June 2027
news.body: VeChain told users on Nov 25 that, as part of Wanchain's transition to community control, WanBridge will stop operating as early as Dec 31, 2026, after which assets can no longer be bridged to VeChain through it. Holders of WanBridge-wrapped assets on VeChain, including wrapped stablecoins, should unwrap them, and a dedicated redemption portal stays open until June 30, 2027; tokens not redeemed by then lose their claim on the underlying assets. Wanchain is also closing XFlows and XPort, while its mainnet continues. VeChain did not name a replacement bridge.
news.why: WanBridge was VeChain's main route to external liquidity under its 2025 Renaissance push, so its loss narrows cross-chain access for VeChain DeFi. Users holding wrapped assets in pools need to act before the deadline.
news.tagReason: Main bridge closing; no replacement named.
news.summary: VeChain told users on Nov 25 that, as part of Wanchain's transition to community control, WanBridge will stop operating as early as Dec 31, 2026, after which assets can no longer be bridged to VeChain through it.

news.title: Braiins discloses BGP route hijacks that diverted hashrate from more than 1,000 bitcoin mining sites
news.body: Mining pool operator Braiins published a security alert on Nov 25 saying an attacker forged internet routes to send miners on plain-text Stratum V1 connections to an impostor pool. On Nov 20 more than a thousand sites across hundreds of networks were redirected in the same second, after smaller episodes in Latin America from Nov 7–12. Braiins says neither its pool nor the miners were breached and pool balances were unaffected; the loss is the redirected hashing work. It calls the attack a live threat to any pool accepting unencrypted Stratum V1 and recommends Stratum V2, certificate-checked TLS, and RPKI route validation by network operators.
news.why: A long-known weakness in bitcoin mining is now being exploited at scale, and the fixes require miners, firmware makers and ISPs to act. It does not affect focus networks directly.
news.summary: Mining pool operator Braiins published a security alert on Nov 25 saying an attacker forged internet routes to send miners on plain-text Stratum V1 connections to an impostor pool.

news.title: Bithumb widens its October breach disclosure: IDs, bank accounts and wallet addresses exposed over 15 days
news.body: Bithumb updated its disclosure on Nov 25 about the October breach of its DaouOffice groupware, saying unauthorized access ran from Oct 12 to Oct 27 rather than about an hour as first reported. Exposed data now includes ID, passport or driver's-licence numbers, bank account details, ID copies, transaction records and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange did not give a revised count of affected people; it is notifying them individually and warned of follow-on phishing. No loss of customer crypto has been reported.
news.why: Leaked identity and wallet data raises the risk of targeted phishing for Korean users, and it lands as Korea's draft law would make exchanges liable for hacks. It is a data breach, not a theft of funds.
news.tagReason: Broader personal-data exposure at a top exchange.
news.summary: Bithumb updated its disclosure on Nov 25 about the October breach of its DaouOffice groupware, saying unauthorized access ran from Oct 12 to Oct 27 rather than about an hour as first reported.

news.title: Fortune: Amazon and Meta are negotiating terms to end Amazon's block on Meta's Muse shopping agent
news.body: Fortune reported on Nov 25 that Amazon and Meta are in talks to restore Muse's access to Amazon's store, which Amazon blocked in September. According to the report, the open issues are how Muse would present Amazon search results, how Amazon's advertising would be handled, and who is responsible for wrong orders and the customer relationship. Any deal would need sign-off from both CEOs, and neither company has confirmed an agreement or timeline.
news.why: Access to Amazon's catalogue is a major test of whether third-party AI agents can shop on the largest US marketplace, and the terms would set a precedent for ads in agentic commerce. It is a reported negotiation, not a deal. No crypto link.
news.summary: Fortune reported on Nov 25 that Amazon and Meta are in talks to restore Muse's access to Amazon's store, which Amazon blocked in September.

news.title: Washington Post: export-banned Nvidia B300 servers are still offered by Shenzhen vendors
news.body: The Washington Post reported on Nov 25 that vendors in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei electronics market said they could supply eight-GPU Nvidia Blackwell B300 servers despite US export controls, quoting about $3 million to $3.4 million, up from roughly $2 million two months earlier. Vendors described stock held in Hong Kong or other off-site warehouses. Nvidia has not been accused of selling the servers directly, and the report does not establish volumes.
news.why: Diversion of controlled chips adds to the export-control scrutiny Nvidia already faces alongside its leadership and accounting reviews. No crypto link.

news.title: South Korea's regulator drafts a full Digital Asset Act: domestic ICOs would return with white-paper filings, won stablecoins get a licence regime and exchange owners face a 20% cap
news.body: South Korea's Financial Services Commission presented the draft 'Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users' at its virtual-asset committee on Nov 24. Token sales to the public would be allowed again if the issuer and others materially involved file a white paper with the FSC before soliciting buyers, with a cooling-off period after acceptance, and exchanges would have to publish disclosures for assets they list. Won stablecoins would need FSC authorization, at least ₩5 billion in capital, 100% reserves held at banks and no interest to holders, with bank-majority consortia allowed to issue first. Exchange shareholders would be capped at 20% (up to 34% with FSC approval) after a three-year grace period, and operators would carry no-fault liability for hacks. The bill still has to pass the National Assembly, and industry groups have already objected to the ownership cap.
news.why: Korea is one of the largest retail crypto markets, so ending the nine-year ICO ban and formalising listing rules would change how new tokens, including focus-list assets, reach Korean users. The ownership cap could force Upbit's and Bithumb's major shareholders to restructure, which is the most contested part of the draft.
news.tagReason: Major draft law; needs National Assembly passage.
news.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission presented the draft 'Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users' at its virtual-asset committee on Nov 24.

news.title: US Justice Department moves to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in frozen USDC from the Binance hack; Circle will reissue tokens after a court order
news.body: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint on Nov 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Oct 29 Binance hack, which US officials attribute to North Korea's Lazarus Group / APT38. The complaint lists 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. Because Circle cannot move tokens out of blocklisted addresses, it agreed to issue replacement USDC once a forfeiture order is entered. Binance separately hired Mandiant, SlowMist and Verichains for independent security reviews.
news.why: It is one of the largest crypto forfeiture actions on record and shows freezable stablecoins becoming the main recovery path after state-linked thefts. Any return still depends on the court process.
news.tagReason: Large recovery path opened; court process pending.
news.summary: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint on Nov 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Oct 29 Binance hack, which US officials attribute to North Korea's Lazarus Group / APT38.

news.title: SBI, SMBC and the Solana Foundation launch SBI Solana Global for stablecoin payments and tokenization in Japan
news.body: SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and the Solana Foundation said they have completed agreements for a three-party joint venture, and SBI R3 Japan has begun full-scale operations as SBI Solana Global. The press release, dated Nov 25 in Japan (Nov 24 US time), names four business lines: stablecoin payment rails including AI-agent micropayments, tokenization of bonds, funds and loan receivables, tokenization of commodities and other real-world assets, and on-chain asset management. The venture plans to build use cases in Japan first, then expand across Asia. No launch dates, products or volumes were disclosed.
news.why: It puts one of Japan's three megabanks and its largest online broker directly behind Solana-based financial infrastructure, adding to the institutional commitments made at Breakpoint. It is an operating framework, not yet a live product, so delivery is the thing to watch.
news.summary: SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and the Solana Foundation said they have completed agreements for a three-party joint venture, and SBI R3 Japan has begun full-scale operations as SBI Solana Global.

news.title: Stellar's Bell upgrade (Protocol 30) passes its validator vote and goes live, adding post-quantum signature checks for smart contracts
news.body: Stellar validators approved Bell, Protocol 30, in the vote that opened at 11 AM CST on Nov 23, and Stellar's Horizon API showed Protocol 30 active on mainnet by 11:26 AM CST. Bell adds muxed contract addresses (a new W-prefixed address that lets one contract or smart account serve many customers), ML-DSA post-quantum signature verification inside Soroban contracts, and millisecond-precision ledger close times. The Stellar Development Foundation says existing contracts keep running untouched, network transaction signatures remain Ed25519, and the upgrade does not itself make ledgers close faster. Wallets, exchanges and indexers had to update SDKs and ledger definitions before the vote; holders needed to do nothing.
news.why: It is the first on-chain step of Stellar's quantum-preparedness plan and makes smart accounts practical for businesses that pool many customers, which fits Stellar's payments and tokenization focus. The practical risk is integrations that missed the new address type or ledger-header format, which could break withdrawals or data readers.
news.tagReason: Major protocol upgrade activated on schedule.

news.body: Hashdex's HYPH11, the first Brazilian exchange-traded fund dedicated to HYPE, began trading on B3 on Nov 24, according to Portal do Bitcoin. It tracks the Nasdaq Hyperliquid Settlement Price Index, is administered by BTG Pactual and charges 0.70% a year, and Brazilian investors can buy it in reais through ordinary brokerage accounts. Hashdex already runs single-asset funds for BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP, and HYPE was already a component of several of its index funds. Separately on Nov 24, Justin Sun publicly asked Hyperliquid to let HTX-linked wallets appeal account restrictions the way MEXC-linked wallets reportedly were; Hyperliquid has not confirmed any review.
news.why: A regulated exchange-listed product widens access to HYPE beyond crypto-native venues, following the Korean won listings earlier this month. It is a non-US fund, so it does not change the US access questions that remain HYPE's main structural limit.

news.title: Solana app-layer incidents: Bullpen's beta-account breach drains about $2.57 million, and Velocity halts all trading over a bug
news.body: Trading terminal Bullpen said it identified unauthorized transfers on Nov 24 involving accounts opened during its April–June 2024 early beta, with a preliminary count of 18–19 accounts including co-founder Ansem's. Ansem said attackers reached his Bullpen profile, which held his Solana wallet's imported private key, and sold his meme-coin holdings; the ANSEM token fell sharply as the wallet sold. Onchain investigators traced about $2.57 million in proceeds to a wallet on Arbitrum, Decrypt reported. Bullpen took the affected test service offline and says other users were not affected; it has not published how access was gained. Separately, Velocity, the Solana perps DEX rebuilt from Drift after its April exploit, paused all transactions on Nov 25 to fix an unspecified bug; it says deposits are unaffected and had not given a restart time.
news.why: Both are application failures, not Solana protocol flaws: one from storing imported private keys, the other from a newly relaunched trading engine. They are reminders to limit balances held in apps that custody keys or run new code.
news.tagReason: Two app-layer incidents on Solana; root causes unpublished.
news.summary: Trading terminal Bullpen said it identified unauthorized transfers on Nov 24 involving accounts opened during its April–June 2024 early beta, with a preliminary count of 18–19 accounts including co-founder Ansem's.

news.title: Upbit and Bithumb flag Sky's SKY and the USDS stablecoin as caution assets and suspend deposits ahead of a Dec 21–24 decision
news.body: Upbit and Bithumb designated SKY and USDS as trading-caution assets at 8 PM KST on Nov 23 (5 AM CST) and suspended deposits on their KRW, BTC and USDT pairs. Upbit cited the credibility, capability and disclosures of the issuing and operating parties; Bithumb cited business substance, sustainability and operator reliability. The move follows a Nov 19 Inca Digital report linking about $518 million of Peg Stability Module flows to wallets tied to hackers and sanctioned actors, which Sky disputes. The exchanges will decide during Dec 21–24 whether to lift, extend or end trading support; USDS has held its peg.
news.why: A delisting of one of the largest dollar stablecoins from Korea's two main exchanges would be a notable compliance precedent for DeFi stablecoins on Ethereum. It is a caution flag, not a delisting.

news.title: Flare puts Confidential Compute on the ballot: FIP.17 would bring TEE-based private computation to mainnet
news.body: Flare Foundation published FIP.17 on Nov 23 and explained it on Nov 24: the proposal would release Flare Confidential Compute (FCC) on mainnet after its Songbird debut under STP.13. FCC lets smart contracts call trusted execution environments that act only when a weighted majority of Flare's data providers relays an instruction and return signed, verifiable results. The mainnet scope includes the core FCC contracts audited by Zellic, FDC-V2 with a TeeAvailabilityCheck attestation type, and verifiable randomness, and new extensions initially need Flare Foundation approval. Flare's blog says voting opens Dec 1, while its X post lists Nov 30–Dec 6; a simple majority is required. On Nov 25 Flare invited community questions ahead of the vote.
news.why: Private but verifiable computation is aimed at institutions that will not put sensitive balances on a transparent chain, and it is the second half of Flare's core design after its data protocols. Foundation-gated extensions at launch are a centralisation trade-off to watch.

weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 4–10, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week's main theme was distribution moving into regulated and mainstream channels. Solana gained Formation's SEC-exemption notice for a tokenized-securities venue, a Schwab Crypto listing, a native privacy layer from Helius and one-tap trading from X cashtags; NEAR Intents went live in Talos's institutional system; HYPE gained won markets on Upbit and Bithumb plus the Elysium L2; and Ondo brought Fidelity's FCAT into every tokenized-stock bridge transfer. Bittensor's Gamma Tokens went live as a protocol payment rail, though first-day use was tiny.

Governance moved from votes to execution. Polkadot enacted Referendum 1966's 500-validator target on Nov 10, while Acala and Karura proposed shutting down in February 2027. Render's RNP-024 closed with only yes votes shown but no official announcement, and the XRPL Foundation's quantum-safe account design remains a draft with a 2027 study.

Security is the cross-watchlist caution. Flare forced an emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, NEAR AI contained a cloud intrusion, and Elliptic traced Binance-hack laundering through NEAR memecoins. Market-wide incidents at Keplr/Web3Auth, LNbits, Ankr, Arcus, Initia and Across were each below the High threshold. Nothing in this recap is a price forecast or financial advice.

stocks.name: Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS)
stocks.overview: Amazon is the parent of AWS, the largest cloud provider, alongside its retail, Prime, advertising, devices and newer businesses (Zoox, Amazon Leo satellites, Pharmacy). In Q3 2026 AWS revenue rose 39% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years and a $184 billion annualized run rate, with $17.8 billion of operating income (38.7% margin). Total net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, operating income was a record $28.1 billion and EPS was $1.89. AWS signed new agreements with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Oracle and others, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17x and Trainium became easier to adopt through TorchNeuron; CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. On Nov 5 Amazon launched $0 Uber Eats delivery for Prime members, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30–Dec 4 in Las Vegas. The main risk is capital intensity: 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion.
stocks.researchSummary: AWS is accelerating on AI demand and is the main driver of Amazon's profits, while retail margins hit a record. The trade-off is very heavy AI capex funded partly with new debt, plus rising data-center permitting risk in the U.S. On Nov 23 Amazon agreed to buy Decart's AI optimization stack and team (reported ~$7.5B) to improve Trainium performance, ahead of re:Invent opening Nov 30. The FAA is probing a Nov 20 Prime Air drone incident in Michigan. Fortune reported Nov 25 that Amazon is negotiating terms to let Meta's Muse agent shop its store again.
